quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Think about what the speaker was looking forward to, and the timing.
quests.explanation: The speaker missed the cake by minutes after waiting all week. Nobody is blamed, so it's disappointment.
quests.textToSpeak: I waited all week for the bakery's new cake. When I got there, the last slice had just been sold.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice how long the speaker has been searching.
quests.explanation: After a long anxious search, the pet is safe and the tension is gone. That's what the clues add up to: relief.
quests.textToSpeak: I've been calling his name up and down this street since noon. There he is, under the car. He's okay!

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen for what the speaker wants explained.
quests.explanation: The speaker wants to understand how something works. The speaker is curious.
quests.textToSpeak: Wait, so this shop sells honey from beehives on its own roof? How do they keep the bees up there?

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Think about how the speaker looks back on their own mistakes.
quests.explanation: Repeating a small slip in front of another person is an awkward memory. Everything points to embarrassment.
quests.textToSpeak: When the waiter told me to enjoy my meal, I said 'you too.' Then I said it again when he brought the check.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice the detail about the brother that the speaker treats as special.
quests.explanation: The family gathering and the little surprise of the brother staying show warm pleasure. That's why happy fits best.
quests.textToSpeak: It's the first time in months that we've all sat around the same table. Even my brother came, and he stayed for dessert.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Focus on why the words won't stay still.
quests.explanation: Losing focus and wanting to close the eyes shows the speaker is worn out. Everything points to tiredness.
quests.textToSpeak: I've read the same page four times, and the words won't stay still. I think I need to close the book, and my eyes.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice what the school said and what it left out.
quests.explanation: The unexplained call about a child leaves the speaker uneasy about what's wrong. That's what the clues add up to: worry.
quests.textToSpeak: My son's school called and asked me to come in today. They said it's not an emergency, but they didn't say what it is.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice what the other person did not ask for.
quests.explanation: A favor given freely and generously makes the speaker want to thank them. This is gratitude.
quests.textToSpeak: You lent me your notes the night before the test, and you didn't ask for anything back. Thank you, really.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to what the speaker chooses to look at.
quests.explanation: Reading the exit sign means nothing in the presentation is holding their attention. Boredom is the feeling here.
quests.textToSpeak: Same slides, same speaker, same jokes as last year. I'm reading the exit sign instead.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Count how many times the speaker has done the same thing.
quests.explanation: A small task that keeps failing is a nuisance rather than a disaster. The speaker is annoyed.
quests.textToSpeak: This is the fourth email telling me to reset my password. It still says 'invalid' every time.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice how long the suitcases have been ready.
quests.explanation: Being packed days early shows how much the speaker is looking forward to leaving. Everything points to excitement.
quests.textToSpeak: Two more days, and then we're on that ship. The suitcases have been sitting by the door since Sunday.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Think about what the watch means beyond telling time.
quests.explanation: The watch is the speaker's last connection to a loved one. Sadness is the natural reading.
quests.textToSpeak: My grandfather's watch stopped working today. It was the last thing he gave me.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice how much time is left and what the speaker's hands are doing.
quests.explanation: Shaking hands just before an important public moment show nervousness.
quests.textToSpeak: The mayor is going to read my name at the ceremony in ten minutes, and my hands won't stop shaking.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to who did the work, and how the speaker judges the result.
quests.explanation: The speaker did it alone and is pleased with how well it turned out. The speaker is proud.
quests.textToSpeak: I fixed the bike myself. No videos, no help. It even rides straighter than before.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to the two statements and how they conflict.
quests.explanation: The speaker has two opposite instructions from the same person. That's confusion.
quests.textToSpeak: She said the deadline was flexible, and then she said it was firm. So which one is it?

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to the pattern of the three questions.
quests.explanation: The speaker is confronting the person who broke a promise, with sharp, accusing questions. Anger is the feeling here.
quests.textToSpeak: You told her my secret? After I asked you not to? Why would you even do that?

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Focus on the second place at the table and on how the meal ends.
quests.explanation: Setting a second place and then eating alone shows how empty the house feels without company. Loneliness is the natural reading.
quests.textToSpeak: Every Sunday the house is so quiet. I set the table for two out of habit, and then I eat alone by the window.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Focus on how the speaker describes the people in the photo.
quests.explanation: Describing a picture full of laughter with such warmth shows the speaker is pleased to see it. Everything points to happiness.
quests.textToSpeak: My sister sent a photo of the whole family at the lake. Everyone's laughing, even Grandpa in that silly hat.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice the length of time and what the speaker is only now learning.
quests.explanation: After ten years, this fact about the neighbor is new to the speaker. That's what the clues add up to: surprise.
quests.textToSpeak: I've lived next door to him for ten years, and today I found out he plays in a jazz band.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice what a very small gesture did to the speaker's morning.
quests.explanation: Being recognized in a small everyday moment lifts the speaker's mood for hours. Simple happiness.
quests.textToSpeak: The bus driver remembered my stop from last week. He said 'Same place?' before I could even open my mouth. It made my whole morning.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to what the speaker notices and what the person says in reply.
quests.explanation: The speaker doesn't believe the reassurance and fears something is wrong. So worried is the best fit.
quests.textToSpeak: She hasn't touched her dinner in three days. She just says she's fine and goes up to her room.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice the repeated action, and the time pressure.
quests.explanation: Repeated attempts that keep failing, with a deadline looming, produce frustration.
quests.textToSpeak: I've refreshed the page ten times. It keeps showing me the same error, and the deadline is at five.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to how the speaker sums up the little things that went right.
quests.explanation: A string of small pleasant moments makes the speaker feel light. Everything points to happiness.
quests.textToSpeak: The train was empty, the sun was out, and my favorite song came on. Today's a good day.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice how the speaker wanted to react after the noise.
quests.explanation: Wanting to disappear after everyone stares shows embarrassment.
quests.textToSpeak: My phone rang loudly in the middle of the silent ceremony. Everyone turned around. I wanted to disappear.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to what the speaker says would have happened without this person.
quests.explanation: The speaker recognizes how much someone's help meant. The speaker is grateful.
quests.textToSpeak: Without your help last month, I would have lost my job. I don't know how to thank you.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Ask why the speaker has been studying the map for so long.
quests.explanation: Over-preparing for a new challenge shows nervousness.
quests.textToSpeak: Tomorrow morning I drive on the highway alone for the first time. I've been studying the map all evening.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice what the speaker wants most at the end of the journey.
quests.explanation: After a long trip, the only thing the speaker wants is to sleep. Everything points to tiredness.
quests.textToSpeak: Three flights, one long delay, and a cold sandwich. I don't care where the bed is. I just need a bed.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to how the speaker says 'it's fine' and whether it sounds convincing.
quests.explanation: The speaker is repeating 'it's fine' to hide let-down over a plan that fell through. The speaker is disappointed.
quests.textToSpeak: We planned this trip for a year, and now work says I can't take the days off. Yeah. It's fine. It's fine.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice what the company did when the speaker complained.
quests.explanation: The company failed and then disrespected the customer, making the speaker feel wronged. That's why angry fits best.
quests.textToSpeak: I paid for express delivery, and it came a week late. When I called, they hung up on me.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Focus on what the speaker was dreading, and how the news changes it.
quests.explanation: A dreaded long trip has been avoided at the last moment. So relieved is the best fit.
quests.textToSpeak: The bridge is open again, so I can take the short way home. I was dreading three more hours in the car.
